attrs.evidence: probe_execclaim_v07_repro.mjs: P-1 reproduces against the frozen v0.6.0 acceptance (JS produces every byte, the caller chooses the label, accept returns ok with implementation_id impl-c-derive-v0.6.0 and trace_conforms true) and 6/6 confined live — the caller cannot select a label at all; provenance is 'observed' only with a host handle and 'unavailable' without one, with NO implementation_id reported in that case; a C claim against an observed JS executor is refused; a C requirement with no observation is refused as unavailable; and an executor handle carries a private Symbol the authority minted so it cannot be fabricated. derive_battery.mjs: provenance-requires-observation, claim-checked-against-observation, executor-handles-are-authority-issued, registered-identity-well-formed, validator-does-not-do-provenance, acceptance-success-shape-narrow. trace_conforms is removed from the acceptance success shape — redundant there, and a boolean per check invites weighing them — while staying in the validator and in the failure diagnostics where semantic_agreement:true + trace_conforms:false is the distinction worth having.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED, and kept as the record of a mechanism that did not do what its own statement said. @2 opened 'AN EXECUTION CLAIM IS NOT PROVENANCE' — which is right and survives into @3 — and then named as its mechanism 'the authority records what it launched via an authority-issued executor handle'. It launched nothing. registerExecutor(implementation_id) took a STRING, put it in a private Map, and returned a handle carrying a private Symbol; the Symbol proved that this authority minted this handle and nothing about any execution. So P-1 did not close, it MOVED: v0.6 let the caller choose the identity at deriveLocally(), v0.7 let it choose the identity at registerExecutor(). And accept(registry, req, res, executor = null) put a proof back in the caller's hands — the exact shape round 17 removed from issuance, one level up — so even a registration that really launched C could have had its handle paired with bytes produced elsewhere. Frozen as P-2 and P-2b in probe_execreg_v08_repro.mjs, which reproduces both against a verbatim frozen copy.
attrs.statement: AN EXECUTION CLAIM IS NOT PROVENANCE. A canonical result arriving from outside is an untrusted execution CLAIM however perfect its bytes are, and no property of the result can establish which executor produced it — not a conforming trace, not a version string, and not a digest of the executable, because a digest carried inside the same untrusted result is self-asserted too. The only thing here that is not a claim is what the HOST OBSERVED IT LAUNCH. So: an implementation's identity comes from the implementation and never from a caller-supplied parameter; validateForeignResult establishes semantic agreement and trace conformance and explicitly NOT provenance, reporting implementation_claimed rather than certifying it; the authority records what it launched via an authority-issued executor handle; and acceptance compares the request's expected_implementation_id against the OBSERVATION, refuses implementation-claim-contradicts-observation when the result's label disagrees with it, and answers implementation-provenance-unavailable — never 'verified' — where no observation exists. Three distinct objects, and round 19's two envelopes were one short: semantic_result is portable MEANING, execution_evidence is the execution CLAIM, and the host's observation is the only OBSERVATION. DECLARED OPEN, now correctly scoped: WHAT identity a native executable should register — a trusted launcher hashing the binary it is about to exec — is unbuilt. WHETHER an independent observation exists at all is no longer optional.
